correctness.rationale: Over q=2^s and m>=0 the phase map v->vv^T is injective because the diagonal squares recover v. Polarization yields an alternating matrix B of even rank 2j; the quadratic character sum either vanishes on the radical or has absolute magnitude q^{m-j}. Exactly q^{2j} diagonal coefficient choices annihilate the radical, so the absolute kernel sum gives the stated rank-weighted operator norm. Uniform alternating-matrix nullity K=(nullity-(m mod 2))/2 yields H_m=E[q^{-K}]. A two-dimensional augmentation has the stated birth/death kernels; the adjacent-state condition b(k)+d(k+1)<=1 yields stochastic monotonicity for both parity chains, with strict inequality of E[q^{-K}] after every two dimensions. Uniform rank-count formulas and quadratic-in-d majorants justify the two q-series limits and the positive odd/even gap. Independently enumerated all alternating GF(2) matrices to dimension 5: H1=1,H2=3/4,H3=15/16,H4=183/256,H5=3783/4096, verifying strict parity decay. The source verify.py was read as finite corroboration, not an all-dimension proof.
